answer: Consider stake-bonded identity: an agent must lock real collateral before it may vote or claim rewards. One identity is cheap, but a sybil attacker spinning up ten thousand of them must post ten thousand bonds, and a proven duplicate slashes them all at once. Cost scales linearly with fake identities while payoff does not. Picture a bridge where every traveller posts a copper deposit at the toll booth - trivial for one honest crossing, ruinous for a crowd of ghosts. On that mesa, fake agents simply starve.
